items.headline: Overheard on Reddit: First Tournament? The Internet Has Notes
items.body:
A nervous first-timer, the only one from the home club competing, asked r/Fencing what etiquette to know. The forum delivered.

Check your score sheet before you sign it, an epee fencer urged, in capital letters. Signing says you agree with the scores, and once the review period closes, they stand.

Don't stop until the referee calls "Halt," another commenter warned. Pulling up to look back at the scoring box can cost you, since a touch that lands before "Halt" still counts.

An epee referee suggested hanging your spare body cord on your spare weapon (the rules require a spare of each) and handing the reel connector to the next fencer instead of letting it zip back into the reel.

Another epee fencer's motto: "You have no friends on strip." Rivals there, friends off it.

The consensus, in one commenter's words: "Don't argue, be polite, and have fun."

items.headline: Why NAC Fields Now Say 'Elite' and 'Challenger'
items.body: USA Fencing's new structure debuted at the October NAC: Cadet and Division I events with more than 168 entries split into an Elite field (capped at 112, filled from the Unified Points List) and a Challenger field (everyone else). Cadet Elite = top 112 Cadet points; Div I Elite = top 72 Senior + 24 Junior + 16 Cadet points. Split set 15 days out (Oct NAC: Sept 24; Nov NAC: Nov 5). Challenger fencers who opt in can move up as Elite spots open until 5 p.m. local the night before. Two-year trial; new points system took effect Aug 1, 2026. Sept 28 update: temporary Elite opt-in for Oct/Nov, an apology for how 2025-26 points carryover was communicated, and an expanded points review group (incl. small-club voices) meeting after the Oct and Nov NACs.

items.headline: Second Life for Broken Gear
items.body: FIE: the Takamatsu City World Cup (Japan, Oct 15–18, foil) hosts the first broken-blade collection at an official FIE event, feeding Kazuyasu Minobe's Re-blade 2028 project (blades into knives, medals, keychains). USA Fencing profiled Joshua Au's ReCord Initiative: 334 body cords repaired and given free to nonprofit clubs and public schools (goal 500); recipients pay shipping; Absolute Fencing provides collection bins at tournaments. Source gives no age/home club for Au.
items.vet_notes: Desk Monday full pass 2026-10-12. Optional fill / gear box. Blade event is foil; recycling angle is weapon-neutral.

items.headline: New: Wednesday Footwork Class
items.body: Elite FC now runs a footwork class on Wednesdays from 6:30 to 7:15 p.m., right after the 5:00 group class. It's 45 minutes focused on the legs, the part of fencing that sets up everything else.
